week.title: FX Daily: Abatement in AI risk helps the dollar
week.desc: Fears of an AI bust have receded slightly, and the AI story has been helped overnight by impressive 3Q results from Korean chipmaker SK Hynix. This has allowed the market to focus on the core story of resilient growth, high inflation and the prospect of higher energy prices – all dollar-positive. Look out for the Fed, the Bank of Canada and the UK budget today

week.title: RBNZ’s huge dovish surprise spells trouble for Kiwi dollar
week.desc: ASIA/PACIFIC: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand surprised with a 4-3 split vote for a hold. While a December hike remains on the cards, the signal was dovish, leaving markets’ tightening expectations vulnerable. That points to further downside risks for NZD vs commodity currency peers, despite potential near-term relief in the undervalued NZD/USD

week.title: FX Daily: Time to think about the midterms?
week.desc: The ECB sent a clear message yesterday: a December hike is likely. That is providing a more supportive backdrop for the euro ahead of today’s 3Q GDP release. Meanwhile, resurgent AI-related jitters and the upcoming US midterms are increasing downside risks for the dollar, in our view, although a still-hawkish Fed argues against major corrections

week.title: Bank of Japan hits 2% price target
week.desc: ASIA/PACIFIC: In a big day for monetary policy in Japan, the Bank of Japan finally announced it had hit its 2% price target – a target set in 2013. The question now for markets is how quickly the BoJ takes the policy rate to neutral. We now think it will hike in December and March. A hawkish BoJ can help keep a lid on USD/JPY at 160

week.desc: At the start of a very busy week for FX markets, the dollar is largely holding onto recent gains. In focus are the US midterms, where betting markets attach a 70% probability to a clean sweep for the Democrats. Away from politics, we'll receive updates on the US jobs market this week and are expecting rate hikes in the UK, Australia and Sweden

week.title: The election will be good news, regardless of outcome, says Morgan Stanley’s chief stock-market strategist
week.desc: Morgan Stanley’s chief stock-market strategist, Mike Wilson, said the midterm elections are a classic “clearing event” whose outcome at this point doesn’t really matter.

week.title: Tech stocks have made big V-shaped rebounds five times in 30 months — and now Deutsche Bank forecasts another bounce
week.desc: Positioning among equity investors in tech stocks is consistent with much slower earnings growth than the sector is achieving. Deutsche Bank thinks it’s time to go overweight once again as the risk-reward profile favors a sector that is suddenly out of fashion.

week.title: UBS’s Fowler Says Market Is Underpricing the Length of AI Cycle
week.desc: Hyperscaler valuations look attractive after the recent AI unwind as the market prices in a shorter AI cycle than is likely to play out, according to Gerry Fowler, chief European equity strategist and head of derivatives at UBS AG.

week.title: Stock Bulls Are Betting on a Bounce After the Midterms

week.title: Citi FX Traders Like Carry But Say It’s No ‘Set-and-Forget’ Bet

week.title: Tech Sell-Off Marks 'Crisis of Confidence,' Says Jordan Jackson

week.title: FX Daily: Democratic sweep can weigh on the dollar
week.desc: We don’t expect today’s US midterm results to cause structural shifts in FX, but the dollar may face some short-term pressure should the Democrats secure both the House (widely expected) and the Senate (close call). Elsewhere, a dovish hike by the RBA has hit AUD, but we remain optimistic on the outlook for the currency beyond the near term

week.title: FX Daily: Blue wave price action a preview of what’s to come
week.desc: For a change, opinion polls proved correct, and the Democrats delivered a stunning victory in the US midterm elections. Short-dated US rates and the dollar are a little weaker, while equity futures are busy reclaiming some of their 2-3% losses seen overnight on fears that the AI data centre build-out would slow. Price action previews what could come in 2027

week.title: Rates Spark: A blue wave in the US and euro inflation
week.desc: A decisive election result supports immediate sentiment, but the prospect of tighter AI regulation could add to jitters about the tech sector. A president now potentially focusing more on foreign policy leaves oil and tariff risks in focus as sources of rate volatility. Eurozone headline inflation is expected to rise to 4%

week.title: A delayed landing for GBP rates
week.desc: EUROPE: GBP rates seem to have drifted too high versus Bank of England expectations, which we attribute to a significant risk premium stemming from prior trading trauma. We therefore see rates lower across the curve, but only once inflation risks settle and US rates ease lower. Meanwhile, structural supply factors will keep the sterling curve steeper

week.title: Euro rates have good reason to be nervous
week.desc: EUROPE: Easing inflation fears should bring euro rates down by mid-2027, but the path lower will be bumpy. We shift our attention from oil to inflation data and expect markets to react anxiously to upside surprises. Rising bond issuance outside the US government and AI could catch markets by surprise, but that is not our base case

week.title: The AI trade has been ‘sold to death’ but Goldman strategist highlights silver lining from Democratic sweep
week.desc: Corporate decision makers may decide to accelerate their plans to expand compute capacity and take advantage of the status quo rather than risk a new administration and different rules in 2029

week.title: Uzbekistan rates stay on hold, but hopes for 2027 cuts remain
week.desc: COMMONWEALTH OF INDEPENDENT STATES: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan kept its policy rate unchanged at 14.00%, as expected, but delivered a more hawkish message than in September. Higher inflation and GDP forecasts suggest that easing in 2026 is now less likely. But we still see scope for cuts in 2027, assuming continued fiscal restraint and potential FX strength
